I had no experience at all, but I thought, “Well, this is important enough that if James loses, I’ll lose too. So why don’t I do my best to win?” I went around the state talking and talking, and I’m sure I did make some good points, but I was never comfortable with it. I was uncomfortable with what I was doing. I didn’t feel I was right. And when James lost, I felt a sense of relief. It was over, and I could go back to practicing law. I was relieved. But looking back, I should have gone out and spoken less. Maybe my speech made the difference, maybe it didn’t, but what I should have done was been more concerned about being right than winning. I’ve learned that lesson. I’ve learned that a man should be able to stand up and say what he thinks, even if it makes his opponent angry, because he knows he’s right.
